profile.campus: San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas (CyrusOne San Antonio campus, SAT4 (inferred))
profile.reading:
Per a dedicated aggregator listing corroborated by CyrusOne's own SAT2-SAT4 campus page, this building (San Antonio IV, inferred to correspond to SAT4 by sequential naming and campus grouping) sits at 9655 Raba Drive, San Antonio, TX 78251, on the shared 295,785 sq ft / 36MW SAT2-SAT4 campus.

CyrusOne's first San Antonio facility opened in 2012; per CyrusOne's own press release on its fifth San Antonio campus (SAT5-SAT6, broken ground January 2025 in Texas Research Park), the company had invested approximately $1 billion in capital to date across its San Antonio campuses as of that release, and describes SAT5-SAT6 itself as two buildings totaling 276,000 sq ft and 36 MW of IT capacity, figures that differ somewhat from an earlier operator-page-sourced figure of 175,000 sq ft/33 MW recorded for that campus elsewhere in this registry, a discrepancy noted rather than silently reconciled. The San Antonio Report, a local nonprofit newsroom, reported in 2026 that the city hosts more than 20 operational data centers with 59 more in various planning stages; CPS Energy, the municipally owned utility, supplies power to 21 of the existing facilities (generating roughly $110 million in revenue) and has projected future data center energy demand in the metro at approximately 26,000 megawatts, while flagging water use as a growing constraint: data centers currently draw about 0.1% of San Antonio Water System's drinking water, but planned new facilities have requested roughly 600 acre-feet of drinking water and 3,000 acre-feet of recycled water against a system that has capacity for only about 10,000 additional acre-feet before requiring upgrades.

CyrusOne's San Antonio growth mirrors a broader pattern across Texas, where absence of a state corporate income tax, relatively low land and construction costs compared to Northern Virginia or Silicon Valley, and CPS Energy's municipal-utility rate structure have made the metro attractive to colocation and hyperscale operators alike; San Antonio's data center footprint has grown alongside comparable buildouts in Dallas-Fort Worth (where CyrusOne's Carrollton facility, opened in 2012, was described by the company as the largest data center in Texas at the time) and Austin.

reading.body:
The individual IT capacity of CyrusOne San Antonio IV is not published. The SAT2-SAT4 campus as a whole, which includes this building, has 36 MW of total IT capacity across 295,785 square feet. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this implies roughly 900 racks across the three-building campus. The campus certifies for SSAE 16 compliance, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and FISMA. The building's physical location in Bexar County places it in a metro area that already operates more than 20 data centers and has over 50 more in planning stages.

San Antonio's data center footprint ranks this metro among Texas's major compute hubs alongside Dallas-Fort Worth and Austin. The published 36 MW for SAT2-SAT4 does not individually rank this facility in the state's top 18 by published capacity. Texas as a whole has 468.41 MW of published data center capacity across 133 mapped facilities, though most facilities publish no specifications. CyrusOne has invested approximately $1 billion in San Antonio data centers over more than a decade and continues to expand, with two additional buildings in planning.

Water availability poses a material constraint on further build-out. San Antonio Water System currently supplies 0.1% of its usage to data centers but has received requests for roughly 600 acre-feet of drinking water and 3,000 acre-feet of recycled water from planned facilities against only 10,000 acre-feet of additional capacity before system upgrades. Power availability is more abundant. CPS Energy, the municipal utility, supplies 21 existing data center facilities and projects metro demand could reach 26,000 megawatts, implying substantial headroom for scaling beyond current campuses if water constraints are resolved.
